lede: One beacon here is fixed: the **Zoltan research facility**, where a Damaged Stasis Pod becomes a Crystal crew member. Everything else is Zoltan bureaucracy — checkpoints, customs sweeps, docking permits, entry fees — and the fights that come out of it are mostly ones you agreed to. Only two of the seven events on the guaranteed-hostile list are actually Zoltan; the rest are pirates, Mantis, a jumpy Engi escort and the Rebel fleet flying under Zoltan flavour text.
callout: **The two lines at risk are the two that make this sector Zoltan.** `NEUTRAL_ZOLTAN` is the checkpoints, the wise man, the docking requests and the briber; `QUESTS_ZOLTAN` is every quest that can start here. Roll high on clouds and hostiles and what is left is a shooting sector with two stores. Roll low instead — the table's floor is 20 slots — and the beacons nobody claimed do not come back to this list; they take generic filler.

section_notes.ZOLTAN_CREW_STUDY: The one beacon the sector must place, and nothing above it can crowd it out. Two of the three ways the scan goes are a polite thank-you and a little scrap; the third is pirates holding the station hostage — two boarders aboard and a pirate ship on the radar. An **Advanced Medbay** trades your medical records for a drone. The **Damaged Stasis Pod** option consumes the pod: they repair it, the crystal inside reassembles, and Ruwen steps out asking to be taken to a hidden wormhole near the Rock home-worlds.
section_notes.HOSTILE_ZOLTAN: Only {{ZOLTAN_FIGHT}} and {{ZOLTAN_ASTEROID}} put an Energy Fighter in front of you — a crew driven mad by deep space, and a guard enforcing mining rights. {{ZOLTAN_PIRATE}}, {{ZOLTAN_MANTIS}} and {{ZOLTAN_ENGI}} are pirate, Mantis and Engi hulls; the last two are the Rebel fleet. Six to eight is also the largest single claim on the map, and it is settled before the three lines under it get a look in.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_ZOLTAN: Where the sector's character actually lives — a security checkpoint, a docking request, a wise man offering you a fight of your choosing in {{ZOLTAN_RIFT_FIGHT}} — and the last line to be filled, so it is the one that pays for a high roll anywhere above. Read {{ZOLTAN_CREW_SCAN}} carefully: submitting can cost a crew member outright, and refusing puts 2–4 Zoltan aboard with your weapons already cut in half.
section_notes.BOARDERS_ZOLTAN: {{ZOLTAN_BOARDERS}} is a customs check that escalates — 3–4 Zoltan aboard and a ship outside. {{ZOLTAN_BOARDERS_MANTIS}} sends 2–3 Mantis with a scout in support. {{BOARDERS_HACKING}} drops 3–5 humans and no ship at all.
section_notes.NEBULA_ZOLTAN: Ten of the fourteen events here arrive through `NEBULA_REBEL`, so most of this block is the generic Rebel nebula pool rather than anything Zoltan. Two to six is a floor rather than a total — the clouds are painted before any other line is filled, and ordinary beacons they cover become nebula beacons drawing from a pool this sector never lists. The standout is {{NEBULA_ZOLTAN_EYE}}: approaching the monolith gives you the **Healing Burst**, a heap of scrap, nothing at all, a fight, or one crew member aged backwards out of existence.
section_notes.ITEM_ZOLTAN: {{ZOLTAN_FREE_MAP}} carries a **Fight** tag it does not earn — the map reveal is free and the Zoltan ship parked at the beacon is loaded non-hostile. It only becomes a fight if you start one.
section_notes.QUESTS_ZOLTAN: Every quest that can begin in this sector begins in this one line, and four of its five entries plant a marker elsewhere on the map — a Mantis war camp, a Federation signal, a derelict worth capturing, and the trade hub. It can also roll zero on its own, before the queue gets a chance to drop it, so there are two independent ways to fly a whole Zoltan sector and never see a quest. A marker you carried in from the last sector is not affected by any of this.

chain.title: Zoltan trade hub · the uncontacted planet

steps.title: {{ZOLTAN_TRADE_HUB}}
steps.detail: Getting inside. Talking your way in can end with 2–4 Zoltan guards following you home and a ship on your tail. A **Crew Teleporter** puts you on the civilian deck unseen; a **Zoltan crew member** just pays the 10-scrap entry fee.

steps.title: A store, or a rumour in the cantina
steps.detail: Once in, it is one of two things: a self-service supply store, or gossip about a newly discovered planet that has never had first contact. Only the cantina continues the chain.

steps.title: {{ZOLTAN_QUEST_PRIMITIVES}}
steps.detail: A Zoltan ship and a Rebel assault craft facing off over the planet. Make first contact yourself and the Zoltan open fire — the Rebel thanks you and tips off the fleet. Shoot the Rebel instead and the Zoltan pay you in weaponry, for old times' sake.

items.text: Of the 18 gated events in the pool, exactly one blue option asks for a Zoltan — the {{ZOLTAN_TRADE_HUB}} entry fee, and it still costs 10 scrap. Flying Zoltan buys you nothing in Zoltan space.
Clean entry to {{ZOLTAN_TRADE_HUB}}, freed slaves at {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} at level 2, plus branches in {{NEBULA_LOST_SHIP}} and {{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}}.
Three graded payoffs inside {{DISTRESS_SATELLITE_DEFENSE}}, and a way out of {{STORM_AUTO}}, {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}} and {{NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}}.
Level 3 turns {{ZOLTAN_CREW_STUDY}} into a free drone; level 2 or 3 saves the man dying on the moon in {{STRANDED_BEACON}}.
Talks the {{ZOLTAN_CREW_SCAN}} guards out of searching you, and reads the madman's intentions in {{STRANDED_BEACON}}.
One drone part digs a Zoltan scientist out of the caves under {{ZOLTAN_ODD_MOON}}.
**Ruwen, a Crystal crew member**, at {{ZOLTAN_CREW_STUDY}} — the guaranteed beacon, if you arrive carrying the Damaged Stasis Pod. The pod is spent doing it.

Zoltan from three places: dug out of {{ZOLTAN_ODD_MOON}}, hired for 40 scrap off {{ZOLTAN_LIFERAFT}} (he may refuse), or handed over by {{ZOLTAN_SCIENCE_DOCK}} after they shoot first and then call it a test you passed.
**Healing Burst** from {{NEBULA_ZOLTAN_EYE}} — the only named item anywhere in this pool.
{{ZOLTAN_FREE_AUGMENT}} is an academy handing one over for nothing. {{ZOLTAN_LIFERAFT}} pays a better one, but only if you clear his ship without destroying it.
Mantis, Rockman or Engi — your pick — out of the hold of {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}}; a human named Charlie from {{STRANDED_BEACON}}.
{{ZOLTAN_FREE_MAP}} reveals the sector for free, on a tour of the ship you are not supposed to be reading the charts on.
Five events in the pool can take a crew member. Two of them — {{ZOLTAN_CREW_SCAN}} and {{NEBULA_ZOLTAN_EYE}} — do it in a way a Clone Bay cannot undo.
Eight events put someone aboard, and three are Zoltan: 3–4 at {{ZOLTAN_BOARDERS}}, 2–4 at both {{ZOLTAN_CREW_SCAN}} and {{ZOLTAN_TRADE_HUB}}.
Refusing to hand over a crew member at {{ZOLTAN_CREW_SCAN}} costs you half your weapons before the shooting starts.

{{PIRATE_BRIBER}} is the only event here that can buy a jump back from the pursuit — and it sits in the line most likely to be cut. {{NEBULA_AUTO_WARNING}} and {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}} each cost you one.

Both fixed stores are settled early enough that nothing can squeeze them out. The two events that can open a shop on top of them — {{PIRATE_BRIBER}} and {{ZOLTAN_TRADE_HUB}} — are in the two lines that get cut, and neither is marked in advance.

Nothing leaks a distress marker in from another line here, so the markers you see are the distress line and nothing else. Eight events can be behind one, two of which can cost a crew member and one of which is {{TRAP_BEACON}}.

Sensors go dark inside one, but this is not a nebula sector, so a cloud beacon halves the fleet's advance for that jump. It is the cheapest delay on the map — and the clouds are drawn before the sector is populated, so their footprint is set before anything else is.
Never one of the beacons below — exits draw from a list shared by every sector. If the clouds happen to cover it, the exit is simply empty.
